N_LABEL_GENES = 10

import base64

```{python}
path_pseudobulk = PSEUDOBULK_FILE
path_manifest = MANIFEST
padj_threshold = float(PADJ_THRESHOLD)
lfc_threshold = float(LFC_THRESHOLD)
n_label_genes = int(N_LABEL_GENES)
max_categories = int(MAX_CATEGORIES)

# padj is floored before the log so that padj == 0 does not produce an infinite y value.
MIN_PADJ = 1e-300

# Columns expected in a pydeseq2 results_df export.
RESULT_COLUMNS = ['feature', 'baseMean', 'log2FoldChange', 'lfcSE', 'stat', 'pvalue', 'padj']
```

---

## <font color='green'>Pseudobulk summary</font>

Counts were aggregated per sample and per group label before testing for differential
expression with pydeseq2. The pseudobulk object below is the input to those tests.

```{python}
adata = ad.read_h5ad(path_pseudobulk)

display(HTML(
    "<p>The pseudobulk data set contains " + str(adata.n_obs) + " pseudobulk profiles and "
    + str(adata.n_vars) + " genes or transcripts.</p>"
))
```

```{python}
def summarise_column(obs: pd.DataFrame, column: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Value counts for one .obs column, returned as a two column table."""
    return (
        obs.value_counts(column)
        .rename_axis(column)
        .reset_index(name='number of pseudobulk profiles')
    )


def describable_columns(obs: pd.DataFrame, max_levels: int) -> list:
    """
    Pick the .obs columns worth tabulating.

    The columns present depend on how the pseudobulk was built (the sample column plus
    whichever columns were used for grouping), so nothing is hardcoded here: any
    non-numeric column with a manageable number of levels is summarised.
    """
    columns = []
    for column in obs.columns:
        values = obs[column]
        if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(values) and not isinstance(values.dtype, pd.CategoricalDtype):
            continue
        n_levels = values.astype(str).nunique(dropna=False)
        if 0 < n_levels <= max_levels:
            columns.append(column)
    return columns
```

```{python}
obs = adata.obs.copy()

# 'pseudobulk_label' is written by the decoupler pseudobulk module and is the most
# informative breakdown when it is there, so it is shown first. It may be absent for a
# pseudobulk object built elsewhere, hence the membership test rather than a direct lookup.
preferred = [column for column in ['pseudobulk_label'] if column in obs.columns]
columns_to_show = preferred + [
    column for column in describable_columns(obs, max_categories) if column not in preferred
]

if not columns_to_show:
    display(HTML(
        "<p>No categorical metadata column with a manageable number of levels was found in "
        "<code>.obs</code>, so no breakdown of the pseudobulk profiles is shown.</p>"
    ))
else:
    for column in columns_to_show:
        table = summarise_column(obs, column)
        html = "<h3><font color='green'>Pseudobulk profiles per " + str(column) + "</font></h3>"
        html += '<font color="black"><details><summary>Click to expand table</summary>'
        html += '<div style="overflow-y: scroll; overflow-x: scroll; max-height: 400px">'
        html += table.to_html(index=False) + '</div></details></font>'
        display(HTML(html))
```

## <font color='green'>Volcano plots</font>

```{python}
display(HTML(
    "<p>Genes are called differentially expressed when <code>padj</code> &lt; "
    + str(padj_threshold) + " and |log2FoldChange| &gt; " + str(lfc_threshold)
    + ". Up- and down-regulated genes are coloured red and blue, respectively; the "
    + str(n_label_genes) + " most significant of them are labelled. Genes with a missing "
    + "<code>padj</code> (filtered out by pydeseq2) are excluded from the plot.</p>"
))
```

```{python}
def read_manifest(path: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Read the headerless three column manifest: filename, group label instance, contrast.

    Grouping comes from the manifest rather than from the file names, because ids may
    themselves contain underscores and would be ambiguous to parse.
    """
    columns = ['filename', 'group', 'contrast']

    if not os.path.exists(path) or os.path.getsize(path) == 0:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=columns)

    try:
        manifest = pd.read_csv(path, sep="\t", header=None, names=columns, dtype=str)
    except (pd.errors.EmptyDataError, pd.errors.ParserError):
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=columns)

    manifest = manifest.dropna(subset=['filename'])
    manifest['group'] = manifest['group'].fillna('NA')
    manifest['contrast'] = manifest['contrast'].fillna('NA')

    return manifest


def read_results(path: str):
    """
    Read one pydeseq2 result table.

    Returns (dataframe, message). Exactly one of the two is None: a missing, empty or
    malformed file yields a message that is reported in place of the plot.
    """
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return None, f"Result file <code>{path}</code> is missing."
    if os.path.getsize(path) == 0:
        return None, f"Result file <code>{path}</code> is empty."

    try:
        results = pd.read_csv(path, sep="\t")
    except (pd.errors.EmptyDataError, pd.errors.ParserError):
        return None, f"Result file <code>{path}</code> could not be parsed."

    if results.empty:
        return None, f"Result file <code>{path}</code> contains no rows."

    missing = [column for column in RESULT_COLUMNS if column not in results.columns]
    if missing:
        return None, f"Result file <code>{path}</code> is missing the column(s): {', '.join(missing)}."

    return results, None
```

```{python}
def volcano_png(results: pd.DataFrame, title: str) -> str:
    """Draw one volcano plot and return it as a base64 encoded PNG."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5))

    padj = results['padj'].clip(lower=MIN_PADJ)
    neg_log_padj = -np.log10(padj)
    lfc = results['log2FoldChange']

    significant = (results['padj'] < padj_threshold) & (lfc.abs() > lfc_threshold)
    up = significant & (lfc > 0)
    down = significant & (lfc < 0)
    rest = ~significant

    ax.scatter(lfc[rest], neg_log_padj[rest], s=6, c='lightgrey', label='not significant')
    ax.scatter(lfc[down], neg_log_padj[down], s=6, c='tab:blue', label='down')
    ax.scatter(lfc[up], neg_log_padj[up], s=6, c='tab:red', label='up')

    ax.axhline(-np.log10(max(padj_threshold, MIN_PADJ)), color='grey', lw=0.6, ls='--')
    ax.axvline(lfc_threshold, color='grey', lw=0.6, ls='--')
    ax.axvline(-lfc_threshold, color='grey', lw=0.6, ls='--')

    labelled = results.loc[significant].assign(_y=neg_log_padj[significant])
    labelled = labelled.sort_values('_y', ascending=False).head(n_label_genes)
    for _, row in labelled.iterrows():
        ax.annotate(
            str(row['feature']),
            (row['log2FoldChange'], row['_y']),
            fontsize=7,
            xytext=(2, 2),
            textcoords='offset points',
        )

    ax.set_xlabel('log2 fold change')
    ax.set_ylabel('-log10 adjusted p-value')
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=10)
    ax.legend(fontsize=7, frameon=False, loc='best')
    fig.tight_layout()

    buffer = io.BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buffer, format='png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
    plt.close(fig)

    return base64.b64encode(buffer.getvalue()).decode('utf-8')
```

```{python}
#| output: asis

manifest = read_manifest(path_manifest)

if manifest.empty:
    print(
        "No differential expression results were produced. Every group was either skipped "
        "by the minimum sample guard or yielded no result table, so there is nothing to "
        "plot here.\n"
    )
else:
    for group, rows in manifest.groupby('group', sort=True):
        print(f"\n### <font color='green'>Group: {group}</font>\n")

        for _, row in rows.iterrows():
            contrast = row['contrast']
            print(f"\n**Contrast: {contrast}**\n")

            results, message = read_results(row['filename'])
            if results is None:
                print(f"\n{message} No volcano plot is shown for this contrast.\n")
                continue

            # pydeseq2 writes NaN padj for independently filtered genes; those points
            # cannot be placed on a -log10 axis and are dropped before plotting.
            n_total = len(results)
            results = results.dropna(subset=['padj', 'log2FoldChange'])
            n_dropped = n_total - len(results)

            if results.empty:
                print(
                    f"\nAll {n_total} gene(s) in <code>{row['filename']}</code> have a missing "
                    "adjusted p-value, so no volcano plot is shown for this contrast.\n"
                )
                continue

            n_significant = int(
                (
                    (results['padj'] < padj_threshold)
                    & (results['log2FoldChange'].abs() > lfc_threshold)
                ).sum()
            )

            image_string = volcano_png(results, f"{group} - {contrast}")

            print(
                f'\n<figure><img alt="volcano plot {group} {contrast}" '
                f'src="data:image/png;base64,{image_string}" />'
                f'<figcaption>{n_significant} of {len(results)} tested gene(s) pass '
                f'padj &lt; {padj_threshold} and |log2FoldChange| &gt; {lfc_threshold}. '
                f'{n_dropped} gene(s) with a missing adjusted p-value were excluded.'
                f'</figcaption></figure>\n'
            )
```

## <font color='green'>Citations</font>

### <font color='green'>[Nextflow](https://www.nextflow.io/)</font>

_Di Tommaso P, Chatzou M, Floden EW, Barja PP, Palumbo E, Notredame C. (2017). Nextflow enables reproducible computational workflows. Nat Biotechnol., 35(4):316-319._

### <font color='green'>[Nfcore](https://nf-co.re/)</font>
This pipelines is a substantially modified version of [nfcore:scdowntream](https://github.com/nf-core/scdownstream), which was originally written by Nico Trummer, and uses [nfcore modules](https://github.com/nf-core/modules):

_Ewels PA, Peltzer A, Fillinger S, Patel H, Alneberg J, Wilm A, Garcia MU, Di Tommaso P, Nahnsen S. (2020). The nf-core framework for community-curated bioinformatics pipelines. Nat Biotechnol., 38(3):276-278_

### <font color='green'>[Scanpy](https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/)</font>

_Wolf FA, Angerer P, & Theis, FJ. (2018). SCANPY: large-scale single-cell gene expression data analysis. Genome Biol., 19(1):15._

### <font color='green'>[decoupler](https://decoupler-py.readthedocs.io/)</font>

_Badia-i-Mompel P, Vélez Santiago J, Braunger J, Geiss C, Dimitrov D, Müller-Dott S, ... & Saez-Rodriguez J. (2022). decoupleR: ensemble of computational methods to infer biological activities from omics data. Bioinform. Adv., 2(1):vbac016._
